title: Empty the sink strainer into the bin
instruction: Empty the food scraps from the sink's drain strainer into the food-waste caddy and put the strainer back in the drain, without letting any scraps go down the drain or onto the counter.
context: Emptying the sink strainer is an everyday kitchen chore. The basket is fished out of the drain by its small knob, emptied over the bin and dropped back into a bore it fits with about a millimetre to spare. While it is out the drain is open, so a scrap dropped in the sink can roll straight down it.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. The table top is the kitchen counter. (1) A stainless steel (20 gauge) top-mount single-bowl kitchen sink set into the counter: rim 63.5 cm side to side and 55.9 cm front to back, standing 3 mm proud; bowl 53.3 cm side to side, 40 cm front to back and 20 cm deep, from 14.8 to 54.8 cm forward, its middle 30 cm right of the centre line. (2) A chrome 3-1/2 in basket-strainer body in the middle of the bowl's floor (34.8 cm forward, 30 cm right): a flange 114 mm across sloping into an 82 mm bore, and a crossbar 49 mm below the floor with a hub (a socket 11 mm across) that the basket's post stands in. (3) In it, a stainless steel strainer basket, 68 g: a perforated cup 79.4 mm across its rolled rim, tapering to 60 mm at its floor and 28 mm deep; a chrome post through its middle with a knurled knob 16 mm across and 9 mm tall whose top is 13 mm above the rim; a black rubber seal 52 mm across under its floor and a 6 mm stem 10 mm long below that, 57 mm overall. Seated, its rim is 5 mm below the sink floor and the top of its knob 8 mm above it. (4) In the basket, nine food scraps (7.9 g in all): two strips of carrot peel (34 x 11 x 1.5 mm, 0.58 g; 30 x 10 x 1.5 mm, 0.46 g), a piece of potato peel (26 x 18 x 1.5 mm, 0.75 g), two peas (8 mm, 0.27 g each), two clumps of cooked rice (two 9 mm lumps, 0.80 g; two 8 mm lumps, 0.55 g), a piece of broccoli floret (a 15 mm head on a 7 mm stalk, 1.2 g) and a piece of apple core (22 x 14 x 12 mm, 3.0 g). (5) A jade-green ABS food-waste caddy (1.8 l, 0.42 kg) with its lid taken off: 22.1 x 12.7 cm at the top, 20.5 x 11.1 cm at the bottom and 9.5 cm tall, standing on the counter with its long side running side to side, its middle 29.5 cm forward and 15.2 cm left of the centre line, 2.4 cm left of the sink's rim. (6) A chrome single-lever gooseneck tap on the sink's back deck (61 cm forward, 30 cm right): 41 cm tall, its spout 25 cm above the deck and reaching 21 cm, swung 50 degrees to the left over the bowl. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end, except the failures, which count at any time. A scrap is in the caddy when its middle is inside the caddy's inner volume, between its walls and below its rim (measured: count the scraps in the caddy). The basket is seated when it is back in the strainer body with its post in the hub: its axis within 4 mm of the drain's, at its seated height within 4 mm, tilted no more than 8 degrees and touching the strainer body (measured: by eye and by touch, the basket sits level in the drain and does not rock). The hands are off when neither gripper touches the basket and each is at least 5 cm from it. 1.0: all nine scraps in the caddy, the basket seated and both hands off it; 0.5: all nine scraps in the caddy; 0.25: at least five scraps in the caddy; else 0.0. 0.0 for good if at any time a scrap goes down the open drain (its middle inside the strainer body's bore, below the sink floor, while the basket is not seated; measured: lift the basket out at the end and look into the strainer body and tailpiece), a scrap lands on the counter or the sink's rim outside the bowl and the caddy (its middle within 15 mm of the counter there; measured: look over the counter), a scrap or the basket falls to the floor, or the basket is dropped (falling faster than 0.6 m/s with no finger on it; judged from the video). The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the basket, the caddy and every scrap still.
reset_notes: Put the nine scraps back in the basket, seat the basket in the drain with its post in the hub, empty the caddy and set it back at its marks.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Stand-ins: the nine food scraps are rigid shapes at real size and mass (masses estimated from volume); they are not soft or sticky. The basket's perforations are drawn; it collides as a cup with 1.5 mm walls (real about 0.5 mm). The counter is the station table, cut out under the sink by the task file. The sink, strainer body and tap are fixed bodies; the caddy's lid is off. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
